title: Nine Streets of Counting
subtitle: 平民与民众 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 平民与民众（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：平民与民众（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：civilian　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 civilian 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1943 my mother was sent to count ① civilian she could not save, and she said the counting was the whole of the lesson. The ② civilian, meaning the person and not the soldier, was nine streets away and was counted by whoever came last; civilian, she said, is the only thing in a war that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ civilian in that street had the same bundle, and the ④ civilian at the end, meaning the one the officer kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly. Civilian, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ civilian was the whole of the peace, meaning the life it carried and not the person. The ⑥ civilian, meaning the life and not any of that, is the only thing in a peace that everybody defends and nobody questions; civilian, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both a person and a life. She said the life is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ civilian had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the bundle. The ⑧ civilian of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine streets and eleven years of counting; civilian, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ civilian I remember is the one at the end, which was counted in 1963 and is still described as the youngest in the county. A ⑩ civilian, my grandmother said in 1968, is the only thing that improves by being counted; every civilian, she said, is a life that has agreed to look like a person. She said the life was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 平民（指那个人本身，与那些士兵相对）
C. 固定搭配：count a civilian 清点一位平民
D. n. 平民（指那条街上每一位）
E. n. 平民（指末尾那一位）
F. n. 平民之生（抽象：它承载的那条性命）
G. n. 那条性命（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The civilian, meaning the person and not the soldier
civilian was the whole of the peace
the civilian had become a number in a report
The civilian of the whole thing
A civilian, my grandmother said in 1968

answers.why: count a civilian 意为“清点一位平民”，1943 年母亲被派去清点她救不了的那位平民。
civilian 意为“平民、老百姓”，指那个人本身而不是那些士兵，隔着九条街，由最后来的人清点。
civilian 指那条街上每一位平民，每一位都是同样的包袱。
civilian 指末尾那一位（军官保留的那一位），是唯一有人认真清点过的。
civilian 意为“平民之生”，抽象指它承载的那条性命，父亲说 civilian 就是那份和平的全部。
civilian 为抽象用法，指那条性命本身，是一份和平里人人都守护、却没人质疑的东西。
civilian 意为“平民、老百姓”，到 1958 年这位 civilian 成了报告里的一个数字。
civilian 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九条街和十一年的清点。
civilian 意为“平民”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1963 年清点过，至今仍被说成全县最年幼的。
civilian 为抽象总称，祖母说一位平民是唯一会因为被认真清点而变好的东西。
